verdicts.title: Sign rank versus VC dimension
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
This work studies the maximum possible sign rank of $N \times N$ sign matrices with a given VC dimension $d$. For $d=1$, this maximum is {three}. For $d=2$, this maximum is $\tildeΘ(N^{1/2})$. verdicts.title: Query-to-Communication Lifting Using Low-Discrepancy Gadgets
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Lifting theorems are theorems that relate the query complexity of a function $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}$ to the communication complexity of the composed function $f \circ g^{n}$, for some "gadget" $g:\{0,1\}^{b}\times\{0,1\}^{b}\to\{0,1\}$. Such theorems allow transferring lower bounds from query complexity to the communication complexity, and have seen numerous applications in the recent years. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a lifting theorem parameterized by low discrepancy and logarithmic gadget length, not by VC dimension of the gadget's row family, and gives no explicit (1/2)·D(f)·d − n bound. It shares the lifting framework but does not address the specific VC-dimension inequality conjectured.
